Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

Diagnosis:
The test sets up a CSVFormat with header detection enabled, a null string set to empty string (""), and instructs the format to ignore empty headers. The CSV input contains empty header fields (empty columns in the header line).

Looking at CSVFormat.withNullString() and withIgnoreEmptyHeaders(), they create new CSVFormat instances setting these parameters accordingly. Parsing the input calls CSVFormat.parse(Reader) which creates a CSVParser.

CSVParser constructor calls initializeHeader(). This method tries to build a header map from format.getHeader(). If the format header array is zero length (which is the case when withHeader() is used without specifying headers), it reads the first record line as the header.

Then it tries to build a map from header names to indices. For each header (line 382), it checks if the header name already exists in the map. It also checks if the header is empty (header.trim().isEmpty()). If duplicate names are found and empty headers are not ignored, an exception is thrown.

However, the empty header handling (line 385) uses header.trim() to check emptiness but does not consider that the header value could be null. Because in CSV files blank fields could be interpreted as null depending on nullString and other parsing logic.

If a header is empty string (""), header.trim() returns "", emptyHeader is true. The key problem is that when nullString is set to "", the parser might set an empty header value to null or vice versa, causing a NullPointerException at header.trim().

The test reproduces a NullPointerException because the header contains empty fields, nullString is "", and withIgnoreEmptyHeaders(true) enabled. The code does not guard against header being a null reference before calling trim(), triggering the exception.

Hence, the root cause is the missing null check before header.trim() call in CSVParser.initializeHeader(). This leads to NullPointerException when empty header field equals null due to the nullString being "".

The stack trace likely originates here due to dereferencing header.trim() when header is null (derived from empty field + nullString combination).

The bug report and test confirm this scenario.

The fix would be to add a null check for header before calling trim() in the initializeHeader method of CSVParser, to gracefully handle null or empty headers when nullString is "" and ignoreEmptyHeaders is true.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
